title: Write the token file, modes, rules and reuse list an agent reads for one brand, and the contrast check that proves it
scenario:
A toy shop, Bramble Toys, is building its app with coding agents. Your teammate wrote the design-system pack the agents will read: the token file, the modes, the rules files, the reuse list and the first contrast check. You review it before the first agent task.

Use the exhibit. The shop, the files and the results are made up for this case. Tool details are from the vendors' pages in October 2026, and the contrast rule is from the W3C page.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Bramble Toys app. One brand, Light and Dark modes.
  Agents: Claude Code and Codex. Design files in Figma.
  Goal: agents build screens from our tokens and our
  components, and every text pair is checked.

TOKENS (bramble.tokens.json, DTCG 2025.10, part):
  "color": {
    "$type": "color",
    "blue-600": { "$value": { "colorSpace": "srgb",
        "components": [0.17, 0.42, 0.69], "hex": "#2b6cb0" } },
    "brand":  { "$value": "{color.blue-600}" },
    "button": { "$value": "{color.brand}" }
  }
  Export test: our design tool exported the file back.
  In the export, color.button is "#2b6cb0", not
  "{color.brand}".

MODES (resolver.json, DTCG Resolver 2025.10, part):
  modifiers:
    theme: contexts light, dark   default: light
    brand: contexts bramble, outlet   (no default)
  Build script input: { "theme": "dark" }

RULES:
  /AGENTS.md
    - Primary buttons use color.brand.
  /apps/outlet/AGENTS.md
    - Primary buttons use color.outlet.accent.
  Note: Codex is working inside apps/outlet.

REUSE:
  Storybook 10, framework @storybook/angular (Webpack).
  .storybook/main.ts: componentsManifest: true
  Storybook MCP addon installed and connected.
  Agent log: no docs-list tool. The MCP page says the
  docs toolset is unavailable.

CONTRAST CHECK (first run, made up):
  Pair                              Size          Script
  white on color.button (Light)     16px regular  5.42:1
  white on color.button (Dark,
    #4a90d9)                        16px regular  3.34:1
  Model note on the Dark pair: "Over 3:1, so it passes."

questions.prompt: TOKENS: the export wrote color.button as a hex. What did the file lose?

options.text: Nothing, because a copied hex keeps the same colour value
options.explanation: The colour is the same today, but the link is gone. A new brand colour would not reach the button.

options.text: Its $type, so the spec says the button token is now invalid
options.explanation: The $type still comes from the color group. The problem is the lost reference.

options.text: The alias: a new brand value will no longer move the button
options.explanation: Right. The spec says tools should preserve references. A copied hex breaks the link to color.brand.

options.text: Its dark mode, since a hex can only hold a Light value
options.explanation: Modes are a separate layer. The export lost the alias to color.brand.

questions.prompt: MODES: the build script passes only { "theme": "dark" }. What should a resolver tool do?

options.text: Build bramble, since it is the first brand in the list
options.explanation: The brand modifier has no default and no input, so the spec says the tool should throw an error.

options.text: Throw an error: brand has no default and no input
options.explanation: Right. The spec says tools should throw an error if an input is not provided; only a modifier with a default can be left out.

options.text: Build Light, since theme has a default of light
options.explanation: The input sets theme to dark, a valid context. The missing input is for brand.

options.text: Build every brand in Dark and let the agent pick one
options.explanation: The spec wants an input for each modifier without a default, not a guess by the agent.

questions.prompt: RULES: Codex works in apps/outlet. Which button rule does it follow, and why?

options.text: color.brand, because the root file is read first and wins
options.explanation: OpenAI says files closer to your current folder override earlier guidance, because they come later.

options.text: color.outlet.accent, since the closer file comes later and wins
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says files closer to your current directory override earlier guidance because they appear later in the combined prompt.

options.text: color.brand, because Codex reads AGENTS.md at the root only
options.explanation: Codex reads project files from the repo root down to the folder you work in.

options.text: Neither, because two AGENTS.md files make Codex skip both
options.explanation: No page says that. Codex combines the files, and the closer one overrides.

questions.prompt: REUSE: componentsManifest is true, but the docs toolset is unavailable. Why?

options.text: The setting is off by default, so it needs a rebuild to switch on
options.explanation: The exhibit already sets componentsManifest: true. The framework is the problem.

options.text: The docs toolset needs a shadcn registry in components.json first
options.explanation: components.json is for shadcn registries. Storybook's docs toolset reads its own components manifest.

options.text: This framework makes no components manifest, so docs tools are off
options.explanation: Right. Storybook lists React, @storybook/angular-vite and @storybook/vue3-vite. For other frameworks, the docs toolset is unavailable.

options.text: Agents may only read manifests through a Figma Code Connect file
options.explanation: Storybook's own MCP server reads its manifests. Code Connect is Figma's separate way in.

questions.prompt: CONTRAST CHECK: the model says the Dark pair passes at 3.34:1. What is right?

options.text: It passes: 3.34 is over 3:1, the line for all button text
options.explanation: 3:1 is only for large text: at least 18 point, or 14 point bold. 16px regular is not large.

options.text: It passes: brand colours are exempt from the contrast rule
options.explanation: Only logo text is exempt. The W3C says brand guidelines do not excuse other text.

options.text: It fails, but only Light needs to pass before the release
options.explanation: Every mode is a look your users see. Run the check, and fix the pair, in Light and Dark.

options.text: It fails: 16px regular is normal text, which needs 4.5:1
options.explanation: Right. Large text is about 24px, or 18.5px bold. Normal text needs at least 4.5:1, and 3.34 is under it.
